detail: Section 8 applies only to Directors and Senior Executives. An employee who is neither is not restricted from margin lending by this policy.

Granting security over APE Securities is not itself a Dealing (Deal means buy, sell, transfer, hedge or otherwise trade) and there is no general encumbrance clause. An encumbrance is regulated only where it forms part of a Margin Loan as defined, in which case prior Board approval and immediate notice to the Chair apply. Security granted to a lender that is not protected from falls in value by a call right over the Securities falls outside the definition and is not addressed.
evidence: Margin Loan means any loan secured against APE Securities where the lender is protected from falls in the value of the Securities by a call right over those Securities.

detail: No encumbrance, pledge or charge restriction applies to Employees who are not Directors or Senior Executives.

There is no general ban on secured financing. Only a Margin Loan as defined is caught, and it is permitted with prior Board approval plus immediate notice to the Chair and consent to public disclosure. The policy does not distinguish vested from unvested Securities as collateral and does not address forced sales by a lender.
evidence: must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

detail: Same Board approval and Chair notification regime as Directors; no other form of secured financing over APE Securities is restricted.
evidence: Any person who is a Director or Senior Executive must not, either personally or through a Related Party, take out a Margin Loan without the prior approval of the Board.

detail: The policy imposes no minimum holding period, no buy/sell window and no prohibition on short-term or speculative dealing.

Entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares is expressly an example of Trading, and AMP Securities expressly include derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to AMP shares, so OTC puts and calls with a bank are squarely covered. A Designated Person must notify the Head of Corporate Governance in writing at least 2 business days before, effect the trade on the second to fifth business day after notification, stay outside black-out periods and hold no Inside Information.
evidence: entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares ... derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any of the above Securities.

detail: No venue distinction is drawn; exchange-traded options over AMP shares are treated identically to OTC derivatives, subject to the same notification, black-out, short selling and 30 day short term trading rules.
evidence: entering into any derivative instrument over AMP shares, and ... agreeing to do any of the above things.

detail: A derivative used to hedge an Equity Instrument held in a Share Plan is caught by the absolute hedging prohibition in 1.7, which applies to all Directors and Employees regardless of Designated Person status and regardless of vesting.
evidence: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan.

detail: Vested Equity Instruments that remain held in a Share Plan (for example subject to a holding lock) cannot be hedged with derivatives until they are withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash. For KMP the Corporations Act imposes the same result independently.
evidence: In addition, the Corporations Act prohibits Key Management Personnel (and their closely related parties) from hedging unvested equity remuneration or vested equity subject to holding locks.

detail: Absolute ban on any hedging arrangement over unvested shares, options, share rights and performance rights held in a Share Plan, applying to every Director and Employee. Breach may lead to forfeiture of Equity Instruments and, in serious cases, termination.
evidence: Directors and Employees must not use any hedging arrangements in relation to shares, options, share rights and performance rights (whether vested or unvested) (Equity Instrument) held in a Share Plan.

detail: The ban runs on vested Equity Instruments for as long as they are held in a Share Plan; it lifts only on the earliest of withdrawal from the plan, conversion to an ordinary AMP share, or conversion to cash.
evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

detail: Once shares are withdrawn from the Share Plan or converted to ordinary AMP shares, the hedging prohibition expressly ceases. Hedging those shares is then an ordinary Trade in AMP Securities: outside a black-out period, with prior written notification to the Head of Corporate Governance, no Inside Information, and subject to the direction and conditions power in 2.4.
evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

detail: An Employee who is not a Designated Person and holds AMP shares outside a Share Plan is not restricted from hedging by this policy; only the insider trading prohibition and the 'can we / should we' reputational test in 1.4 apply.
evidence: This prohibition ceases to apply in respect of any Equity Instrument acquired through a Share Plan from the time it is withdrawn from the plan, converted to an ordinary AMP share or converted to cash (whichever is the earliest).

detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar structure is Trading because it involves granting or disposing of a beneficial interest in AMP shares or a right to dispose of them, and because AMP Securities include derivatives entered into with a third party, so the 2.4 notification and black-out rules apply. If it is held in a Share Plan the 1.7 hedging ban bites first.
evidence: granting, acquiring or disposing of any beneficial interest in AMP shares (or any option or other right to acquire or dispose of AMP shares)

detail: Outright ban, defined narrowly as selling borrowed financial products with a view to repurchasing them later at a lower price. A cash-settled short derivative position is not obviously within that definition, but would still be Trading requiring notification.
evidence: Short selling of AMP Securities by Designated Persons is prohibited.

detail: Section 2.9 is confined to Designated Persons; the policy is silent on short selling by other Employees.

Securities lending is not addressed. Borrowing is mentioned only in the descriptive definition of short selling in 2.9; lending out AMP shares is not prohibited or named, though a transfer of beneficial interest would be Trading.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives entered into with a third party in relation to AMP shares and so AMP Securities; trading them requires 2.4 notification and falls outside black-out periods, and in practice the 30 day short term trading ban in 2.8 would prevent most CFD activity.
evidence: derivatives entered into with a third party over or in relation to any of the above Securities.

detail: Absolute ban for AMP Limited directors on entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities. The ban is on maintaining as well as entering, so pre-existing arrangements must be unwound, and there is no approval or exceptional circumstances route out of 2.7.
evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

detail: Same absolute ban as for AMP Limited directors, covering entering into and maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.
evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

detail: Designated Persons who are not AMP Limited directors or Executive Committee members are warned against, but not prohibited from, margin lending over or in respect of AMP Securities. The warning is grounded in forced sale risk during a black-out period, and the policy states clearance to sell in a black-out period to meet a margin lending arrangement would not likely be granted.
evidence: AMP warns all other Designated Persons against entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities due to the risk of forced sale of those Securities during a black out period, in breach of this policy.

detail: Section 2.7 sits within the additional restrictions for Designated Persons; Employees who are not Designated Persons are not addressed.

Granting security over AMP shares is not named, but granting a beneficial interest in AMP shares, or a right to dispose of them, is an express example of Trading, so a share mortgage or charge in favour of a bank should be notified under 2.4 and taken outside a black-out period. For AMP Limited directors and ExCo members an encumbrance that forms part of a margin lending arrangement is prohibited outright by 2.7.
evidence: granting, acquiring or disposing of any beneficial interest in AMP shares (or any option or other right to acquire or dispose of AMP shares)

detail: The policy does not address the use of unvested Share Plan entitlements as collateral; in practice they are unable to be dealt with while held in the plan and any risk-reducing arrangement over them is caught by the 1.7 hedging ban.

Only margin lending arrangements are expressly banned, but the wording 'over or in respect of AMP Securities' is broad enough to capture a bank loan secured on AMP shares with lender protection against price falls. Other forms of secured financing are not separately addressed and there is no general secured financing clause.
evidence: prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

detail: Identical prohibition to AMP Limited directors; no waiver mechanism is provided and section 3 exceptional circumstances relief is directed at black-out period trading, not at 2.7.
evidence: Directors of AMP Limited and members of the Executive Committee are prohibited from entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities.

detail: For other Designated Persons the policy contains only a warning, not a prohibition, on margin lending, and says nothing about other secured financing over AMP Securities.
evidence: AMP warns all other Designated Persons against entering into or maintaining any margin lending arrangement over or in respect of AMP Securities

detail: A hard 30 day buy to sell (or sell to buy) window measured from the last buy until a sell of a Security of that class or type. Successive buys or successive sells within 30 days are unrestricted. Carve-out for trading shares acquired on the exercise of options or the exercise or vesting of performance or share rights under a Share Plan.
evidence: Designated Persons must not engage in short term trading (ie 30 days or less) in AMP Securities. The 30 days applies from the last time an AMP Security is bought until an AMP Security of that class or type is sold (or vice versa).

detail: The 30 day rule applies only to Designated Persons.

Flat prohibition on using Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities, on the stated rationale that they would allow value to be realised even if performance hurdles are not met. Derivatives takes its section 761D meaning and expressly extends to any arrangement that limits the economic risk of an unvested holding.
evidence: AGL Employees are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities.

detail: The permission for Derivatives over vested AGL Securities is conditional on the Securities not being subject to a holding lock, so vested but holding-locked shares (for example under AGL's Employee Share Plan) cannot be collared.
evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy (including approval requirements) and the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.

detail: Derivatives over vested, unlocked AGL Securities are expressly permitted subject to the Policy's approval requirements, and paragraph 4.2 puts the point beyond doubt for Designated Persons. Securities includes Derivatives as defined in section 761D and financial products under section 1042A with no venue limitation, so an OTC put and call with a bank is within scope. Approval is discretionary, withdrawable without reason and valid for one week.
evidence: For the avoidance of doubt, this requirement includes any proposed dealing in Derivatives in respect of fully vested AGL Shares.

detail: Exchange traded options and warrants are expressly identified as Securities in the Purpose section, and are treated no differently from OTC derivatives: prior written approval, outside blackout periods, no inside information, no holding lock and compliance with the short-term dealing ban.
evidence: The definition of Securities is complex but includes shares in a company and derivative instruments such as exchange traded options and warrants.

detail: An AGL Employee who is not a Designated Person needs no approval to deal in Derivatives over vested, unlocked AGL Securities, but must still stay outside blackout periods, hold no inside information, satisfy the Front Page Test and comply with the short-term dealing, short selling and secured financing prohibitions.
evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy

detail: Hedging of unvested holdings is caught both by the ban on Derivatives over unvested AGL Securities and by the anti-avoidance limb of the Derivatives definition, which sweeps in any other arrangement operating to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding or that in combination would confer a greater benefit than would otherwise have been realised.
evidence: any other arrangement which operates to limit the economic risk of an unvested holding in AGL Securities

detail: Vested AGL Securities subject to a holding lock fall outside the permission in 3.6 and so cannot be hedged with Derivatives; the exceptional circumstances route in 5.1 is also expressly unavailable for Securities subject to a restriction on disposal.
evidence: the AGL Securities are not subject to a holding lock.

detail: Hedging vested, unlocked AGL Securities with Derivatives is expressly permitted for Designated Persons with prior written approval from the person set out in the 4.2 matrix, executed within the one week approval validity and outside blackout periods.
evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested, provided any dealing in those Derivatives complies with the other requirements of this Policy (including approval requirements)

detail: Non-Designated employees may hedge vested, unlocked holdings without approval, subject to the blackout periods, insider trading rules, Front Page Test and the 3.4 short-term dealing ban.
evidence: AGL Employees may use Derivatives in relation to AGL Securities which have vested

detail: Monetisation is not named. A prepaid forward or similar is a dealing because it acquires or disposes of an economic interest and involves granting a right or obligation to dispose of Securities, so it requires prior written approval. Any monetisation funded by a loan for which AGL Securities may be used as security is separately prohibited by 3.7.
evidence: granting, accepting, acquiring, disposing, exercising, or discharging an option or other right or obligation to acquire or dispose of the Securities.

detail: Absolute ban on short selling for all AGL Employees, described as borrowing a security and selling it in the hope of buying it back at a lower price to close out the short position.
evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities.

detail: Stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities are banned outright for all AGL Employees, with no approval route. This removes the ability to lend the collared shares to the bank or to support any borrow-based structure.
evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into short selling or stock lending arrangements in relation to AGL Securities.

detail: CFDs are not named but are Derivatives within section 761D and so Securities. Over vested unlocked shares a Designated Person would need prior written approval, but in practice a CFD would be difficult to reconcile with the ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis, and a short CFD would engage the short selling ban.
evidence: AGL Employees must not deal in AGL Securities as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis.

detail: A CFD referencing unvested AGL Securities is a Derivative in relation to unvested AGL Securities and so within the flat 3.6 prohibition.
evidence: AGL Employees are not permitted to use Derivatives in relation to any unvested AGL Securities.

detail: Margin loan arrangements are prohibited for every AGL Employee, both where they fund the acquisition of AGL Securities and where AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment. There is no approval, exceptional circumstances or grandfathering carve-out. Arrangements such as margin loans that could result in disposal within 3 months of acquisition are separately banned by 3.4.
evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

detail: Granting security is not itself defined as a dealing, but 3.7 prohibits any arrangement in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as security against repayment of a loan. The prohibition is drafted at the level of possible use as security, so even a facility under which the shares merely may be charged is caught. An encumbrance unconnected with any loan is not addressed.
evidence: or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

detail: The ban extends beyond margin loans to 'other secured financing arrangements', applies to all AGL Employees and their Connected Persons where practicable, and is not limited by vesting state, tier or amount. No approver is given power to waive it and the exceptional circumstances regime in 5.1 addresses only disposals during blackout periods.
evidence: AGL Employees are prohibited from entering into margin loan arrangements (and other secured financing arrangements) to fund the acquisition of AGL Securities or in relation to which AGL Securities may be used as a security against repayment of the loan.

detail: Two limbs: a general ban on dealing as a short-term trader or on a speculative basis, and a hard 3 month holding period from acquisition that also catches entering into arrangements (margin loans are the stated example) which could result in the Securities being disposed of within 3 months. Carve-outs for securities from options or rights held at least 3 months, shares acquired under an AGL employee equity plan, and share rights under a pro rata entitlement offer.
evidence: AGL Employees who acquire AGL Securities must not dispose of those Securities, or enter into arrangements (such as margin loans) which could result in those Securities being disposed of, within 3 months of acquisition.

detail: No express derivatives rule for vested holdings. Dealing expressly extends to forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities, and to agreements to do any of those things, so an OTC put and written call are Dealings. A Designated Person may therefore enter them only inside a 30-day Trading Window, with written Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer valid for five trading days, and only if not in possession of Inside Information.
evidence: Dealing in Securities is a broad concept and covers more than simply buying or selling Securities. It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities.

detail: Exchange-traded options over Ansell shares are Securities (the definition expressly includes options and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market) and are treated identically to OTC derivatives: Trading Window plus five trading day Clearance.
evidence: The definition of securities in the Corporations Act is very broad, and includes shares, options, debentures, convertible notes and any other financial product able to be traded on a financial market.

detail: Writing put or call options over the underlying Securities and Dealing in derivative products are expressly named as prohibited conduct for all participants in an approved share or equity plan while the plan Securities remain unvested. The ban applies to every plan participant, not only Designated Persons.
evidence: Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products or entering into other arrangements intended to hedge a 'profit' in those Securities.

detail: Purpose-based prohibition on any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value of a plan security and remove the element of price risk while it remains unvested. The list of prohibited conduct is expressly non-exhaustive, so economically equivalent structures are caught.
evidence: All participants in an approved share or equity plan of the Company are prohibited from engaging in any conduct that seeks to secure the economic value attaching to a security granted under the relevant plan and remove the element of price risk inherent in the value of those Securities, while the Securities remain unvested.

detail: Clause 5.3 is keyed to Securities that 'remain unvested' and clause 5.2 separately refers to 'the end of applicable vesting or restriction periods', so plan shares that have vested but are still within a restriction period are not expressly covered by the hedging ban. The underlying plan rules, which are not part of this Policy, would need to be checked.

The clause 5.3 hedging prohibition stops at vesting, and hedging Securities is expressly a Dealing. Hedging vested, unrestricted shares is therefore permitted for a Designated Person inside a Trading Window with Clearance from the relevant Authorising Officer, subject to the front page test which is an express ground for refusing approval.
evidence: It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities.

detail: An employee who is not a Designated Person and whose plan securities have vested is not restricted by clause 5.3 and is not subject to Trading Windows or Clearance; only the insider trading prohibition and the front page test apply.
evidence: while the Securities remain unvested.

detail: Monetisation is not named, but forward contracts are expressly within the definition of Dealing, so a prepaid forward or similar requires a Trading Window and Clearance. If the monetisation is funded by a loan or similar funding arrangement in respect of Ansell Securities, clause 4.8 says a Designated Person should not enter into it.
evidence: It extends to subscribing for the Company's Securities, forward contracts, granting options and hedging Securities. It also extends to entering into an agreement to do any of the above.

detail: The Policy contains no short selling prohibition and does not use the term; a short sale would still be a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and Clearance for a Designated Person, and would sit uneasily with the short-term dealing ban.
Securities lending is not mentioned anywhere and is not listed in the definition of Dealing.

CFDs are not named. They are derivative products over Ansell Securities and so a Dealing requiring a Trading Window and Clearance, but the clause 4.6 prohibition on short-term trading, including within 3 months of receiving Securities, would in practice preclude typical CFD activity.
evidence: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities

detail: A CFD over unvested plan securities is Dealing in a derivative product that removes price risk and is expressly prohibited conduct under clause 5.3.
evidence: Prohibited conduct includes, but is not limited to, writing put or call options over the underlying Securities, Dealing in derivative products

detail: A one-line prohibition covering margin loans and 'similar funding arrangements' in respect of Ansell Securities, with no vesting-state or amount qualification. It is expressed as 'should' rather than 'must', and clause 4.5 gives Authorising Officers discretion to approve Dealings that would otherwise be prohibited by the policy, so a waiver route is arguably available.
evidence: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.

detail: Clause 4.8 sits within the additional restrictions for Designated Persons and does not apply to other employees.

Granting security over Ansell Securities is not named and is not listed in the definition of Dealing. The Policy nevertheless contemplates that security agreements over Ansell Securities exist, since clause 4.4(a)(v) treats a disposal resulting from a secured lender exercising rights under a loan or security agreement as an Excluded Dealing. An encumbrance forming part of a margin loan or similar funding arrangement is caught by clause 4.8.

Clause 4.8 reaches beyond margin loans to any 'similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company', which on its face captures a bank loan drawn against and secured on Ansell shares as part of a collar. There is no dedicated waiver in clause 4.8 itself, but clause 4.5 permits an Authorising Officer to approve Dealings otherwise prohibited by the Policy.
evidence: No Designated Person should enter into a margin loan or similar funding arrangement in respect to Securities in the Company.

detail: No secured financing restriction applies to employees who are not Designated Persons.

No short-term trading, including trading within 3 months of receiving the Securities, except in limited circumstances (severe financial hardship, dealings of long term incentive Securities upon vesting, or a legal obligation to sell or transfer) and with the approval of the Company Secretary.
evidence: No Designated Person should Deal in Ansell Securities on a short-term trading basis, including trading in Ansell Securities within a 3 month period of receiving the Securities

detail: A flat prohibition on Designated Persons and their Associates entering into Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, not just plan securities and regardless of vesting. Hedging arrangement is defined by economic effect, capturing any transaction designed to limit exposure to economic risk in securities. Paragraph 16 provides an exemption route only for dealing outside a Trading Window in Exceptional Circumstances and for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 11b (collateral), not for 11d, so there is no approval pathway for hedging.
evidence: Additionally, Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).

detail: Non-executive directors and the CEO are Designated Persons, so the flat 11d hedging ban applies to them and to their Associates over any Endeavour Securities, including shares acquired on market outside any plan. No exemption route exists: paragraph 16 reaches only trading window exemptions and prohibited dealings under 11b.
evidence: Designated Persons are: non-executive directors, the CEO and the Company Secretary of Endeavour ... Additionally, Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities

detail: Executive Committee members and their direct reports are Designated Persons and are therefore subject to the same flat prohibition on Hedging arrangements in relation to any Endeavour Securities, with no approval pathway.
evidence: Executives Committee members and their direct reports; ... Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities

detail: The 11d hedging ban applies directly to Associates of Designated Persons, and the Designated Person is responsible for making them aware of it and taking reasonable steps to ensure compliance, so a collar cannot be routed through a spouse, controlled entity or trust.
evidence: Designated Persons and their Associates must not: ... enter into Hedging arrangements in relation to Endeavour Securities, including those specified in paragraph 9 (no hedging).

detail: Plan participants and their Associates must not hedge unvested Endeavour Securities allocated under an equity-based remuneration plan. This applies to every participant, whether or not they are a Designated Person.
evidence: If you participate in an Endeavour equity-based remuneration plan you (or your Associate) must not enter into any Hedging arrangement in respect to any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

detail: The paragraph 9 ban expressly extends to vested plan securities that remain subject to a dealing restriction, so a holding lock keeps the shares out of reach of any collar.
evidence: must not enter into any Hedging arrangement in respect to any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

detail: Paragraph 9 stops at vested securities that are free of any dealing restriction, so a plan participant who is not a Designated Person may hedge vested unrestricted plan shares, subject only to the insider trading prohibition and the market perception obligation.
evidence: any unvested Endeavour Securities or vested Endeavour Securities which are subject to a dealing restriction, allocated to you under that plan.

detail: A team member who is neither a Designated Person nor an equity plan participant is not caught by either hedging prohibition; only the insider trading prohibition and the market perception obligation apply, and there is no Trading Window or clearance requirement.
evidence: There are additional obligations which apply to Designated Persons and their Associates and to participants in Endeavour's equity-based remuneration plans.

detail: The definition of derivative expressly names collars, together with options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps and contracts for difference, and defines them by their function of limiting the economic risk of holding securities. A purchased put plus written call over Endeavour shares is therefore a Hedging arrangement banned by 11d for Designated Persons and their Associates, with no venue limitation and no approval route.
evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

detail: Exchange-traded options and warrants over Endeavour Securities are treated identically; in addition paragraph 11c separately bans dealing in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities within a six month period.
evidence: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain).

detail: The derivative and hedging restrictions in paragraph 11 apply only to Designated Persons and their Associates, and paragraph 9 only to equity plan participants, so an ordinary team member dealing in derivatives over their own vested unrestricted shares is not restricted by this policy.
evidence: There are obligations in this policy that apply to Endeavour Group and to all team members. There are additional obligations which apply to Designated Persons and their Associates and to participants in Endeavour's equity-based remuneration plans.

detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structure is a forward contract and a transaction that operates to limit economic risk, so it is a Hedging arrangement prohibited by 11d. evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

detail: Short selling is not named anywhere in the policy. A short sale by a Designated Person would still be a dealing requiring a Trading Window and clearance, would engage the six month rule, and a synthetic short would be caught by the hedging ban.

Stock lending is expressly within the definition of deal, so it is not prohibited as such but must occur inside a Trading Window with written clearance from the relevant approver, executed within three business days. There is no separate stock lending prohibition.
evidence: Deal includes to: ... margin lend, stock lend or make other financing arrangements for securities

detail: Contracts for difference are expressly named in the definition of derivative, which is framed as a product or transaction operating to limit economic risk, so CFDs over Endeavour Securities are Hedging arrangements banned by 11d, and are separately caught by the six month rule in 11c.
evidence: Any product (such as options, forward contracts, swaps, futures, warrants, caps, collars and contracts for difference) or transaction that operates to limit the economic risk associated with holding securities.

detail: Margin lending using Endeavour Securities as collateral is a prohibited dealing under 11b, but the December 2022 revision added an express clearance process: under 16b a Designated Person or Associate may seek approval for a prohibited dealing under 11b, submitting written details of the securitisation arrangement concurrently to the CLO and Company Secretary as endorsers and the Board Chair and the Chair of the Audit, Risk & Compliance Management Committee as approvers, who may grant, refuse or make it conditional in absolute discretion without reasons.
evidence: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy

detail: Paragraph 11 applies only to Designated Persons and their Associates; the policy is silent on margin lending by other team members.

evidence: use Endeavour Securities as collateral in any financial transaction, including any margin lending arrangements (no security or margin lending), unless otherwise permitted under this policy

evidence: an approval for a prohibited dealing under paragraph 16b then you must provide written details of the securitisation arrangement and any other information requested by Endeavour.

detail: The collateral ban and its clearance process sit within the Designated Persons obligations and do not reach other team members.

A six month buy/sell window applying both to the same Endeavour Securities and to derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities. The only carve-out is the exercise of rights under an equity-based remuneration plan and the subsequent dealing of those securities in accordance with the policy.
evidence: deal in the same Endeavour Securities, or in derivatives issued over Endeavour Securities, within a six month period (no short term gain). detail: Flat prohibition on trading in CWY derivatives by Directors and Employees, expressed to apply to all CWY securities and not limited by venue, so an OTC put or call written or bought with a bank over CWY shares is caught. detail: Once full and unrestricted title has passed and the incentive has been achieved, clause 6 is spent; hedging of freely held shares, and of shares never acquired through an incentive plan, is not prohibited. Any such derivative is nonetheless a 'trade' requiring prior written consent from the Company Secretary and cannot be entered during a No Trade Period.
evidence: Before trading the Company's securities, persons covered by this Policy must, in writing: (a) notify the Fletcher Building Limited Company Secretary of their intention to trade in securities, and receive consent to do so

detail: Monetisation, prepaid forwards and similar structures are not named. An agreement to sell is expressly a trade, so a forward sale or collar-plus-loan monetisation of unrestricted shares needs prior written consent, valid 10 trading days, and must be outside a No Trade Period. Monetising equity incentive awards that are still at risk would breach clause 6.
evidence: 'trade' includes buying or selling listed securities, or agreeing to do so

detail: Short selling is not mentioned anywhere in the Policy or its Schedules. A short sale would still be a 'trade' requiring consent, but there is no express prohibition.
Securities lending and borrowing are not mentioned, and the definition of 'trade' (buying, selling, agreeing to do so, and trading in derivatives) does not obviously sweep in a stock loan.

CFDs are not named. A CFD is a derivative which relates to Fletcher Building securities and so is a 'trade' requiring prior written consent. If the underlying exposure is equity incentive remuneration still at risk, clause 6 prohibits it outright.
evidence: trading in derivatives (such as options or warrants) over or which relate to Fletcher Building securities

detail: Margin lending is not mentioned. There is no prohibition, no notification obligation and no guidance on forced sales by a margin lender during a No Trade Period.

Granting a mortgage, charge, lien or pledge over Fletcher Building securities is not mentioned and is not within the definition of 'trade', which is confined to buying, selling, agreeing to do so and trading in derivatives.

Secured financing in respect of Fletcher Building securities is not addressed at all: no prohibition, no clearance requirement, no disclosure trigger. The loan leg of a funded collar is therefore not caught by the Policy, though the security granted must not itself effect a disposal requiring consent.
There is no minimum holding period, no speculative or short-term trading ban and no LIFO or intention test. The only temporal constraint is that a consent lapses 10 trading days after notification.
